commit.author: Carl Boettiger <cboettig@gmail.com>
commit.message:
Stop giving provider URLs to the CRAN URL check (#126)

The incoming check on the 0.3.0 submission reported https://www.itis.gov/
as a 404 from inst/doc/data-sources.html. The URL is correct -- it serves
200 from every network, user agent and method tried -- so the 404 came from
ITIS's own CDN. That does not help: a chance 404 during the incoming check
routes the submission to manual review and costs a round trip with the
maintainers, whatever the page actually serves.

So the vignette no longer names a URL for any provider. The table names
each one, and the home page, licence and preferred citation come from
taxadb_provider_info() at runtime, where the check does not resolve them.

The ITIS citation is bibliographic rather than its DOI on purpose: a bare
doi: in a vignette *is* harvested and resolved (two already are, from the
same file), and doi:10.5066/F7KH0KBK redirects to www.itis.gov, so citing
the DOI would have inherited the same flakiness.

Two links that were genuinely dead, which the check never sees but users
do, are fixed in passing: itis.gov/what_itis.html was renamed (citation.html
is the page stating CC0), and the Catalogue of Life citation pointed at
doi.org/10.48580/dfz8, which is gone -- COL mints a DOI per release, so any
pinned one rots.

The new url-check workflow runs urlchecker monthly against the built
package, so inst/doc HTML exists to check, and against the provider URLs
held in R strings. It tolerates the 403s that GBIF, FishBase and
SeaLifeBase return to automated clients, and rechecks once before failing,
since a single hiccup is the thing being defended against rather than a
reason to go red. It stays off the pull request path for the same reason.
